title: Budget
description: Five amounts for every category, always separate: what you estimated, what you committed, what was invoiced, what you paid and what you now expect it to cost.
closedNotice: The occasion is closed. The budget is read-only.

hero.label: Paid to date, {date}
hero.noEstimate: The total estimate is still unknown.

figures.forecastUnknown: Fill in the forecast per category.

table.title: By category
table.caption: Budget by category: estimate, committed, invoiced, paid and forecast
table.legend: You fill in Estimate and Forecast. Committed, Invoiced and Paid are worked out from expenses and supplier bookings.

bars.title: Estimate by category
bars.note: The largest category is highlighted. Categories without an estimate are not shown.

categories.presetsLegend: Usual categories for this kind of occasion
categories.presetsHint: Pick the ones that fit. You can rename them at any time.
categories.name: Category name
categories.estimateHint: What you planned to spend. Leave empty if you do not know yet.
categories.forecastHint: What you now expect it to cost. Leave empty if you do not know yet.
categories.removeConfirm: Delete the category “{name}”? Its expenses stay and move to “No category”.
categories.emptyTitle: You have no budget categories yet
categories.emptyBody: Start with the usual categories below or add your own.

expenses.title: Expenses
expenses.emptyBody: Add the first receipt or invoice. Approval and payment are tracked separately.
expenses.receiptRetention: Receipts and invoices are kept for {years} years after the occasion is closed, as bookkeeping rules require.
expenses.amountLocked: The amount of a paid expense changes only through a correction.
expenses.deleteConfirm: Delete the expense “{name}”? It cannot be recovered.
expenses.independent: Approval and payment are independent: an expense can be approved without being paid, and paid without being approved.
expenses.approvalManagersOnly: Only the owner or the project manager approves expenses.

correct.title: Correction to a paid expense
correct.intro: A payment is a fact: it is not overwritten. The correction keeps the old value, the new value, the reason and who made it.
correct.amountHint: Leave unchanged if the amount was right.
correct.reasonHint: For example: “I mistyped the amount on the receipt”.

alerts.title: Money to watch
alerts.overrun: {category}: the forecast is {amount} over the estimate
alerts.moreOverruns: and {count} more categories over their estimate

export.title: Budget (CSV)
export.description: The five amounts for every category, for Excel or your accountant.

errors.amountRequired: Enter an amount greater than zero, for example 1,250 or 1250.50.
errors.amountInvalid: The amount is not a valid number. Enter for example 1,250 or 1250.50.
errors.categoryExists: You already have a category with this name. Choose another name.
errors.categoryMissing: The chosen category no longer exists. Choose another.
errors.tooManyCategories: You can have at most {limit} budget categories.
errors.receiptMissing: The receipt was not found. Upload it again.
errors.paidAmountLocked: The expense is paid, so its amount can no longer be edited directly. Use “Correct the payment” and give the reason.
errors.paidCannotDelete: A paid expense is not deleted. If the payment was recorded by mistake, use “Correct the payment”.
errors.correctionNotPaid: The expense is not paid, so you can edit it directly, without a correction.
errors.correctionNothing: Change the amount or tick that it was not paid.
